text:
Matvei Michkov scored twice for PHI, and the first one came with the man advantage in the opening period, a snap shot at 7:41 that the data gave about a 22 percent chance of going in. PHI had the better of that period by a wide margin, creating chances worth 1.92 expected goals (a measure of shot quality) to 0.75 for COL. Michkov added a second snap shot at 12:23 of the second, a 4 percent look that the model rarely rewards.

COL pushed back from there. The Avalanche took 68 shot attempts to 50 for PHI, and they outscored PHI 0.95 to 0.50 in expected goals in the third. Martin Necas pulled COL within one late in the second on a 4 percent chance of his own, and T.J. Hughes cut it to 3-2 at 14:40 of the third. In between, Noel Acciari tipped in a third PHI goal at 6:34, and Trevor Zegras, who set up all three PHI goals other than Michkov's first, finished with three assists.

By deserved-to-win, which is the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, PHI came out ahead at 58 percent to 42 percent, so the 3-2 result fit the play. Joseph Woll saved 24 of 26 shots and stopped the best chance COL had, a 31 percent look for Artturi Lehkonen in the first. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 21 of 24 and finished slightly behind what the shots called for.
